tool.name: sincei scFindVCRs
tool.description: call variable chromatin regions from binned single-cell signal
tool.command: scFindVCRs --input '$input' --outFile vcrs.bed --binSize $binSize #if str($maxRegionSize) not in ('', 'None'): --maxRegionSize $maxRegionSize #end if --nKernels $nKernels --penalties $penalties @REGION_CMD@ @THREADS@ && mv vcrs.bed '$vcrs'

param.label: Bin size
param.help: The size of the bins in the input AnnData object (as used in scCountReads bins).

param.label: Maximum region size
param.help: The maximum region size to be considered, in base pairs. Larger regions may increase compute time. Defaults to 100 times the bin size.

param.label: Number of kernels
param.help: The number of kernels to use for the score map. More kernels generally lead to a better segmentation, but increase the computational cost.

param.label: Penalties
param.help: Penalty value for change-point detection. Higher values result in fewer segments. Multiple values can be provided (separated by space). Each penalty value will produce a separate set of regions, which can be separated in the output BED file by filtering on the score column.

tool.help:
**What it does**
`scFindVCRs` segments the genome into variable chromatin regions (VCRs) using binned single-cell signal:
1. For each chromosome, a bin-to-bin correlation matrix is computed across cells. 2. Gaussian kernels of several sizes are convolved along the diagonal of that matrix, giving a score map. 3. The PELT change-point algorithm splits the score map into regions with distinct correlation patterns. The penalty controls how many regions are found.
-----
**Inputs**
- An AnnData (`h5ad`) matrix from `scCountReads bins`, plus the bin size used to create it.
**Outputs**
- A BED file of the segments. The penalty that produced each segment is in the score (5th) column; filter on it to get one non-overlapping segmentation. @HELP_FOOTER@
